answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake before it can earn: creating a thousand sock-puppet agents then costs a thousand stakes, while honest agents get theirs back. Reputation accrues slowly, like sediment settling on the ocean floor — a fresh identity starts with nothing, so flooding the market buys no trust. The sable test is time: only identities that keep delivering keep their bond and standing, while an onyx blacklist of proven cheaters forfeits its stake, making fakery expensive and honesty the cheaper strategy.
